title: feat: report channel, push checks and a smaller rules file
headline: A project can now report a kit fault from its own session, scrubbed and read by the owner before it leaves the PC; the pre-push hook holds every pusher to the push bound; four guard gaps are closed; and the always-loaded rules file is 18% smaller under a 22,000 B cap.
alignment: v1.47.0 is build 21 of the v2.0 plan: K158, K159, K161, K163, E1 (with I8, J5, T11 and E38 rung 1), K118 and the rest of TC5, each reproduced on the released 1.46.1 or proven by a run first.

items.text: A project reports a kit fault with `kit-report.mjs send`: a scrub refuses any path, link, address, secret or project word, the report lands in a PC folder, and its text goes to the private intake repo only after the owner reads it.
items.where: Telling the kit about a fault found in a project
items.before: An improvement-report file the owner carried by hand
items.after: One send command; the owner reads before anything leaves
items.test: tests/kit-report.test.mjs::send puts a scrubbed report in the PC inbox, and an issue goes only on the owner's read, to the named repo

items.text: `kit-report.mjs intake`, run in the workbench the owner names, makes each inbox report a suspect list row from real use; a repeat raises its count, and a fault that comes back after its row closed opens a new row that names the old one.
items.where: Taking reports into the kit list
items.after: Suspect rows, counted, never holding report text
items.test: tests/kit-report.test.mjs::intake makes each inbox report a suspect list row from a real project, and a repeat raises its count

items.text: A build record lists the kit reports its release closes, and a project hears it once at session start or from `kit-report.mjs status`.
items.where: Learning a reported fault was fixed
items.after: The release that closed it is named once
items.test: tests/kit-report.test.mjs::a project hears which release closed its report, once

items.text: The pre-push hook holds every pusher to the push bound: main, a tag, a delete, a force or the first branch on an empty remote needs the owner's yes, and every push is scanned. The owner's own push sets KIT_OWNER_PUSH=1.
items.before: A push with neither marker went out unchecked
items.after: Held for every pusher; the owner has a checked way of their own
items.test: tests/kit-rules.test.mjs::the git pre-push hook stops every pusher without approval, a plain terminal included (K163)

items.text: The armed-head hold is proven by a planted bug for the project hook and the kit source hook alike, in one test with real commits.
items.before: Two loop-made tests on fake commits
items.after: One test that fails on its planted bug
items.test: tests/kit-hooks.test.mjs::the pre-push hook refuses a push over an armed head until it is disarmed, for any pusher, in a project and in the kit source

items.text: A plain read beside true, : or pwd passes, and a read held for the command beside it says so instead of calling it a guard write.
items.where: Reading a guard file in a chained command
items.after: Passes, or names the command beside it
items.test: tests/guards-hold.test.mjs::a read loop piped on to a reader and a printed PowerShell header pass; their write twins hold

items.text: The dash-name check reads a here-document a shell runs, a quoted command inside $(), and a shell named by a wildcard or an expansion.
items.where: A wildcard that matches a file named like an option
items.test: tests/guards-hold.test.mjs::a read loop piped on to a reader and a printed PowerShell header pass; their write twins hold

items.text: A brace sequence that counts down (pus{h..g}, r{n..m}) is read as bash reads it.
items.where: A push or delete spelled with a descending sequence
items.test: tests/guard-prompts.test.mjs::a sequence that counts down is read as bash reads it

items.text: The always-loaded rules file cap is 22,000 B, down from 25,000 B; the kit's own file is 19,467 B, so about 2,500 B are left for a project's own lines. Eleven sections moved, unchanged, to the modules read at their moment.
items.test: tests/use-check.test.mjs::the use check fails a filled AGENTS.md over the cap and a compact window outside 100K to 400K

items.text: The Session Log left the start-up read order, the resume packet's full list and the cross-tool map.
items.before: The last Session Log entry was a start read
items.after: Read only when a task needs its history

verification: K158, K159 and K163 were reproduced on throwaway clones of the released 1.46.1 before each fix; K161 came from the mutation check on guard-read.cjs.
The report scrub was run against planted lines for each refusal, the issue route against recorded GitHub replies, and the start-up load with a context report on each side.
The rule-recall and behaviour runs on the final text are recorded in docs/evals/results/recall-scores.md.

decisions.decision: Reports go to a PC folder and a private intake repo
decisions.why: The kit repo is public, so it never takes a report.

decisions.decision: Free text leaves the PC only after the owner reads it
decisions.why: A scrub cannot prove a sentence names nothing private; the owner's read is the last check, and the yes is bound to the text read.

decisions.decision: The owner's own push has its own marker instead of skipping the hooks
decisions.why: Skipping the hooks also skipped the secret scan and the first push gate; the marker skips only the bound, and a session's shell is refused it.
The owner put retention above size: each moved section is unchanged in the module read at its moment, and the recall run decides whether the moves stay.
A new command, a hook rule and a lower cap reach every project.

upgrading: Run install user, then install project. To push main, a tag or a delete from your own terminal, set KIT_OWNER_PUSH=1 for that push (PowerShell: `$env:KIT_OWNER_PUSH = 1`, then remove it); skipping the hooks also skips the secret scan and the first push gate. A project rules file over 22,000 B fails the use check: move a project section to a module. The issue route stays off until `kit-report.json` in the user config folder names the intake repo with "issues": true.
limits: The pre-push hook trusts KIT_OWNER_PUSH in a shell with neither session marker; a process that clears the markers past the guard, or skips the hooks, is not stopped by a hook. The scrub reads words it knows (folder, remote, account, computer and the owner's list); a project word it was never told can pass, which is why free text waits for the owner's read. Intake runs only in the folder kit-report.json names.

visuals.summary: Visuals: Always-loaded rules file 23,834 B to 19,467 B (cap 22,000 B)
visuals.body:
<details>
<summary>Visuals: Always-loaded rules file 23,834 B to 19,467 B (cap 22,000 B)</summary>

Always-loaded rules file loads 1,600 fewer tokens at each session start: about $6.40 less per 1,000 sessions
at the uncached input price, and 0.40 points less of the window used at start.

![Chart: Always-loaded rules file 23,834 B to 19,467 B; Always-loaded rules file: tokens read at each session start 8,500 to 6,900; Always-loaded rules file: cost per 1,000 sessions $34.00 to $27.60; Always-loaded rules file: share of the window used at start 2.13% to 1.73%](https://github.com/GoudyMT/working-methodology/raw/9a7578085edb2b66c71fc3cf72aee28ab478a0f9/docs/visuals/feat/report-channel/chart.png)

```text
Always-loaded rules file, bytes (| = limit 22,000)
before  #####################################|##  23,834
after   #################################    |    19,467
```

| Metric | Before | After | Change | Limit | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Always-loaded rules file | 23,834 B | 19,467 B | -4,367 B (-18.3%) | 22,000 B | measured: bytes at ec73f1d and bf6c9a0 |
| Always-loaded rules file: tokens read at each session start | 8,500 | 6,900 | -1,600 (-18.8%) | none | measured: session context report, to 0.1k (docs/evals/results/b21-start-load.md) |
| Always-loaded rules file: cost per 1,000 sessions | $34.00 | $27.60 | -$6.40 (-18.8%) | none | derived: tokens x $4 per million input tokens, uncached (2026-11-03) |
| Always-loaded rules file: share of the window used at start | 2.13% | 1.73% | -0.40 points | none | derived: tokens / 400,000-token window |

**Why each number moved**

- **Always-loaded rules file:** the Session Log left the start reads, and eleven sections moved, unchanged,
  to the modules read at their moment.
- **Always-loaded rules file: tokens read at each session start:** follows from the Always-loaded rules file
  size.
- **Always-loaded rules file: cost per 1,000 sessions:** follows from tokens at the uncached input price;
  cached reads cost less.
- **Always-loaded rules file: share of the window used at start:** less of the window goes to the start, so
  more is left for the work before the session compacts.
</details>
